2027-05-29.title: Saturday of the first week after Pentecost · St Theodosia
readings: Appoint elders in every town: a bishop, as God's steward, must be blameless
Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple
2027-05-29.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the First Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam remembers St Theodosia; it does not say which saint of that name is meant. Tomorrow, the Second Sunday after Pentecost, is Vocations Day.
2027-05-29.verse: Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
theo: Tomorrow our Church keeps Vocations Day, and today's Epistle could hardly be more fitting. St Paul has left his co-worker Titus on the island of Crete with a task: “I left you behind in Crete for this reason, so that you should put in order what remained to be done, and should appoint elders in every town, as I directed you.” The young churches of Crete needed shepherds, and Paul did not leave the choice to chance. He lists what such a man must be: “For a bishop, as God's steward, must be blameless; he must not be arrogant or quick-tempered or addicted to wine or violent or greedy for gain; but he must be hospitable, a lover of goodness, prudent, upright, devout, and self-controlled.” Then the most important quality: “He must have a firm grasp of the word that is trustworthy in accordance with the teaching, so that he may be able both to preach with sound doctrine and to refute those who contradict it.” From the beginning the Church has been built on the apostles and on those they appointed to succeed them. St Ignatius of Antioch, writing on the way to his martyrdom, told the Christians of Smyrna: where the bishop appears, there let the people be, just as where Jesus Christ is, there is the Catholic Church (Letter to the Smyrnaeans 8, in substance). Our own Church has lived this through every generation, from the first bishops to those who shepherd us today.

Paul's list is demanding, and it is meant to be. A bishop is called “God's steward”: the household is not his, it belongs to God, and he will give an account. But the list is also a mirror for every Christian. Hospitality, goodness, prudence, self-control, a firm hold on the faith: these are not only for bishops and priests. And they are learned first at home. Where do priests and religious come from? From families where the evening prayer is kept, where the Qurbono is the centre of Sunday, where a child sees a father who is not quick-tempered and a mother who loves goodness, where the priest is welcomed and prayed for. If our parishes lack vocations, the first question is not about seminaries but about our homes. Tomorrow, on Vocations Day, pray by name for the young people of your parish, and ask whether God may be calling someone in your own family. And pray for the priests and bishops we already have, that they may be the stewards Paul describes.

The Gospel tells us the price of every vocation, lay or ordained. “Now large crowds were traveling with him; and he turned and said to them, ‘Whoever comes to me and does not hate father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters, yes, and even life itself, cannot be my disciple. Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.’” The word “hate” is a Semitic way of speaking about what comes first; St Matthew gives the same saying as loving father or mother “more than me” (Matthew 10:37). Jesus does not ask us to stop loving our families; he asks that no love, not even love of our own life, be placed above him. The Imitation of Christ calls this the royal road of the holy Cross, and says that in the Cross is life and protection from our enemies (Book II, 12, in substance). The Panchangam today remembers St Theodosia. It does not tell us which of the holy women of that name is meant. One whose story is well attested is Theodosia of Tyre: Eusebius of Caesarea records that during the persecution of 307 a young Christian girl from Tyre, not yet eighteen, went up to the confessors who were on trial at Caesarea, greeted them and asked them to remember her when they came before the Lord; for this she was arrested, cruelly tortured and drowned in the sea (The Martyrs of Palestine 7, in substance). Whether or not she is the saint our Church names today, her courage shows what the Gospel means: she loved Christ more than her own life, and she carried the cross to the end.
outline: Ask: what comes first in my life, before even my family and my own life?
Paul sends Titus to give the young churches shepherds.
The bishop's virtues are a mirror for every home where vocations are born.
Point 3 · Carry the cross and follow
The price of discipleship, and the courage of a young martyr named Theodosia.
“Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.”
live: Tomorrow, on Vocations Day, pray by name for two young people of your parish and for your parish priest.
Name one thing you love that has begun to come before Christ, and give it its right place this week.
2027-05-29.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Good Shepherd, you sent your apostles to appoint shepherds in every town. Give your Church bishops and priests after your own heart: blameless stewards, hospitable and self-controlled, holding firm to your trustworthy word. Bless our families, so that from them may come men and women ready to serve you. Give us the grace to love you above all things and to carry our cross each day behind you. Through the prayers of St Theodosia and all who loved you more than their own lives, keep us faithful to the end. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: The shepherds whom the apostles appointed stand at the altar in every generation: through the bishop and the priests the one sacrifice of Christ is offered, and the flock is fed with the Body of the Lord who carried his cross for us.

quick: Paul left Titus in Crete to appoint elders in every town; a bishop, as God's steward, must be blameless and hold firm to the trustworthy word.
Jesus: no one who puts anything, even life itself, above him can be his disciple.
Whoever does not carry the cross and follow him cannot be his disciple; St Theodosia's name recalls the martyrs who loved Christ more than life.
2027-05-29.action: Pray today for vocations to the priesthood and religious life from your own parish.
2027-05-29.question: Is there anything I love more than Christ?

family.explain: Jesus said that to be his disciple we must love him even more than our family and our own life, and we must carry our cross and follow him. This does not mean we stop loving our parents or brothers and sisters. It means Jesus comes first, and when we put him first, we learn to love everyone better. Tomorrow is Vocations Day, when we pray for priests and sisters.
family.intention: We pray for our priests and for young people whom God is calling to serve him.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one cross each of us can carry for Jesus this week without complaining?”

illus: A parish priest in a village near Kollam kept a small framed photograph of a family in his office: a farmer, his wife and their five children standing in front of a small house. When people asked about it, he said it was his own family, taken the year before he entered the seminary. He would point to the corner of the photo, where a calendar of saints hung on the wall behind them, and say: my father prayed the evening prayer under that calendar every night, even after the worst day in the field. I learned there what a steward of God looks like. I only took it to the altar.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, give your Church shepherds after your own heart, and teach us to carry our cross and follow you. Amen.
share: Appoint elders in every town (Titus 1:5). Which priest has shaped my faith, and have I thanked God for him?
He must be hospitable, a lover of goodness, prudent, upright, devout, and self-controlled (Titus 1:8). Which of these virtues do I most need?
Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple (Luke 14:27). What is my cross at present?
pm.resp: Lord, send labourers into your harvest.
interc: For our bishops and priests, that they may be blameless stewards of God's household.
For young people whom God is calling to the priesthood and religious life, that they may answer with generosity.
For Christian families, that they may be the first seminary where vocations are born.
For those who suffer for their faith, that like the martyrs they may carry the cross with courage.
For our parish, that on Vocations Day tomorrow many may hear God's call.
pm.close: Father, you sent your apostles to appoint shepherds for your people. Give us bishops and priests after your own heart, make our homes places where vocations grow, and grant us to love your Son above all things and follow him with our cross. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, tomorrow is Vocations Day, and St Paul speaks to us about shepherds. He left Titus in Crete so that you should put in order what remained to be done, and should appoint elders in every town (Titus 1:5). The Church has always needed shepherds, and she still does.

Paul says: for a bishop, as God's steward, must be blameless (Titus 1:7). He must be hospitable, a lover of goodness, prudent, upright, devout, and self-controlled (Titus 1:8). He must hold fast to the trustworthy word. These virtues are also for each of us, and they are learned first at home. Good priests come from homes where prayer is kept and the Qurbono is loved.

In the Gospel Jesus tells the crowds the price of following him: whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple (Luke 14:27). He does not ask us to stop loving our families. He asks to be loved first, above everything, even above our own life.

Today we remember St Theodosia. The Panchangam does not tell us which saint of that name is meant, but the martyrs who bore that name loved Christ more than their own lives. Let us pray tomorrow for vocations, let us thank God for our priests, and let us carry our own cross behind Jesus with love. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said that if we want to be his friends and followers, we must carry our cross. What does that mean? It means doing the right thing even when it is hard: being kind to someone who is not kind to you, helping at home when you would rather play, telling the truth when you are scared. Tomorrow is Vocations Day. Maybe Jesus is calling one of you to be a priest or a sister one day! Let us pray for that.

intro: Theme: “Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.”
On Saturday of the first week after Pentecost, the eve of Vocations Day, with St Theodosia: shepherds for every town, the virtues of God's steward, and the cross of every disciple.

sub: The apostles and those they appointed.
Where the bishop is, there let the people be.
q: I will give you shepherds after my own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.
tend the flock of God that is in your charge, exercising the oversight, not under compulsion but willingly
points.apply: Thank your parish priest this week, and pray for your bishop by name.

sub: A household that belongs to God.
q: It is good for one to bear the yoke in youth
Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it.
points.apply: Keep the family evening prayer every day this week, and include a prayer for vocations.

sub: Christ loved above all, even above life.
The royal road of the holy Cross.
A young martyr who asked to be remembered.
q: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his faithful ones.
But they have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, for they did not cling to life even in the face of death.
points.apply: Accept one daily cross this week without complaint, and offer it for those who suffer for their faith.

concl: The Church lives by the shepherds God gives her, and they grow from homes where Christ comes first.
Every vocation passes along the road of the Cross, and the martyrs show that it leads to life.
2027-05-29.resolve: Pray for vocations, love Christ above all, and carry your cross behind him.
